title: Peering fanout reconciliation race causing orphaned resolver bindings
creator: Ava Chen
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent cross-tenant hostname resolution after a VPC peering failover. Investigation shows a race during peering fanout reconciliation where resolver bindings (egress resolver -> tenant namespace) are left in an orphaned state. Orphaned bindings sometimes get reattached to the wrong tenant context on subsequent reconciliation attempts, causing DNS responses to surface from an incorrect resolver and violating tenant isolation guarantees.

root_cause_summary: Reconciliation applies peering fanout updates with non-atomic removes; when cleanup races with re-attachment, resolver binding entries can remain referencing the old resolver instance and later be inadvertently associated with a different tenant egress namespace.
proposed_fix: Introduce a reconciliation generation token per peering epoch, ensure fanout apply/remove operations carry the token, add idempotent teardown that only removes bindings matching the current generation, and run a GC pass post-reconciliation to evict orphaned resolver entries.
rollback_plan: If the rollout causes regressions, revert the runtime change and re-enable emergency mitigation (TTL reset + full rebuild on peering change). Rollback target: 15 minutes to revert and redeploy older runtime binary.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR and run full canary (5%). 2) Expand to 25% after 6h with zero regression. 3) Expand to 60% after 12h. 4) Full rollout across Dedicated regions. 5) Post-rollout GC sweep and verify metrics remain stable.
verification_steps: A) Synthetic: Repeat peering flip test harness (1000 tenants) and assert 0 cross-tenant DNS hits. B) Prod: Monitor resolver-hit mismatch, tenant egress associations, and customer RPS on enqueued DNS errors. C) Run tenant isolation e2e smoke for three largest affected customers.
